description: err-20260828T144849-I60TAU incorrectly concluded the shared-shell cwd had self-healed back to the IES root after a stray `cd systems/eval-harness/runs/` broke a hook invocation. It had not: `pwd` just now (after a Write tool call) showed the shell was STILL in systems/eval-harness/runs, roughly two hours and many Bash calls later, and the same hook-blocking failure recurred on the next PostToolUse hook invocation.
correction: Ran `cd` explicitly back to the IES root and verified with `pwd` before continuing. Retracting the prior entry's claim that the issue was transient/self-resolving — it was not; the cwd only appears stable between incidents because hook failures only surface when a hook actually fires, not continuously.
systemic_fix: Never assume a shared-shell cwd issue has resolved just because the next command happened to succeed. Verify with an explicit `pwd` check, and treat any stray `cd` in this session as a standing risk until root is explicitly confirmed.
